topic: Bounded LLM assessment for beginner prose

sources.title: LLM-Rubric: A Multidimensional, Calibrated Approach to Automated Evaluation of Natural Language Texts
keyInsights: Independent rubric dimensions plus human calibration substantially reduced judge error.
Human raters themselves differ, so raw model labels require task-specific calibration.

sources.title: Learning to Judge: LLMs Designing and Applying Evaluation Rubrics
keyInsights: Generated rubrics can be interpretable while remaining model-dependent.
Internal consistency can coexist with poor human alignment on factual criteria.

sources.title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
keyInsights: Response order can reverse model judgments.
Prompting a judge to ignore order does not reliably remove position bias.

sources.title: Humans or LLMs as the Judge? A Study on Judgement Bias
keyInsights: Judges can prefer polished presentation and fake authority over factual quality.
Evaluation sets need confident, well-written misconceptions and fake-reference attacks.

sources.title: JudgeBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Based Judges
keyInsights: Objective hard negatives expose judge failures hidden by preference benchmarks.
Evaluation must measure conceptual error detection rather than preference for nicer prose.

sources.title: LLMs instead of Human Judges? A Large Scale Empirical Study across 20 NLP Evaluation Tasks
keyInsights: Agreement varies by criterion, task, annotator expertise, and text source.
No single judge or reasoning prompt dominates across evaluation properties.

sources.title: Evaluating the Evaluator: Measuring LLMs' Adherence to Task Evaluation Instructions
keyInsights: Additional rubric detail yields limited gains when model priors dominate.
Operational criteria need direct adherence tests rather than prompt-length assumptions.

sources.title: Rating Roulette: Self-Inconsistency in LLM-As-A-Judge Frameworks
keyInsights: Identical prompts and settings can produce low intra-rater reliability.
Determinism does not guarantee human agreement, so stability and correctness need separate measures.

sources.title: Trust or Escalate: LLM Judges with Provable Guarantees for Human Agreement
keyInsights: Selective evaluation can improve human agreement when calibrated on representative labels.
Verbalized and token-probability confidence are not reliable abstention signals by themselves.

sources.title: Concord: An Agreement-Aware Multi-Adjudication Pipeline for LLM-as-a-Judge
keyInsights: Inter-judge disagreement can identify useful human-review cases.
Panel gains do not automatically transfer across domains or response formats.

sources.title: The Power of Feedback Revisited: A Meta-Analysis of Educational Feedback Research
keyInsights: Feedback has a positive average effect with substantial heterogeneity.
Information content strongly moderates whether feedback helps.

sources.title: Focus on Formative Feedback
keyInsights: Useful formative feedback is supportive, timely, specific, and manageable.
Grades, normative comparison, person praise, and excessive complexity can distract from the task.

sources.title: Effects of Feedback in a Computer-Based Learning Environment on Students' Learning Outcomes
keyInsights: Elaborated feedback outperformed correctness-only feedback.
Higher-order outcomes especially benefit from explanation of the relevant relationship.

sources.title: A Review of Feedback Models and Theories: Descriptions, Definitions, and Conclusions
keyInsights: Feedback should connect current state, target state, and a route forward.
Learner uptake is part of the feedback process rather than an optional afterthought.

sources.title: Inducing Self-Explanation: a Meta-Analysis
keyInsights: Self-explanation prompts have positive average effects across tasks and subjects.
The learner should perform the causal explanation before a completed explanation is revealed.

sources.title: Feedback Both Helps and Hinders Learning: The Causal Role of Prior Knowledge
keyInsights: Feedback effects depend on the learner's existing strategy and knowledge.
Already-correct reasoning should receive less interruption and explanation.

sources.title: Exploring Teachers' Informal Formative Assessment Practices and Students' Understanding
sources.publisher: Journal of Research in Science Teaching
keyInsights: Formative assessment is a cycle of eliciting, recognizing, using, and rechecking evidence.
A judgment without an opportunity to revise leaves the cycle incomplete.

sources.title: The Use of Scoring Rubrics: Reliability, Validity and Educational Consequences
keyInsights: Analytic topic-specific rubrics and rater training can improve reliability.
A rubric alone does not establish that the resulting judgment is valid.

sources.title: A Chain-of-Thought Prompting Approach with LLMs for Evaluating Students' Formative Assessment Responses in Science
keyInsights: Student-response judges can overfit keywords, miss synonyms, and reuse faulty evidence.
Human-supervised error analysis remains necessary even with detailed reasoning prompts.

sources.title: Teacher Feedback to Improve Pupil Learning
keyInsights: Feedback should establish the learning intention, the current gap, and a forward action.
Instruction must include a plan for how the learner will use feedback.

sources.title: Use Amazon Bedrock API Keys
keyInsights: Bedrock API keys can authenticate direct HTTPS requests through an Authorization Bearer header.
The bearer token must stay out of arguments, logs, webview state, and persisted learner records.

sources.title: Structured Model Outputs
keyInsights: Strict JSON Schema can require fields, close objects, and constrain enums.
Structured output still requires handling refusals, truncation, and semantic mistakes.

sources.title: Evaluation Best Practices
keyInsights: Fixed classification criteria are easier to evaluate than open-ended impressions.
Human calibration, adversarial cases, and continuous evaluation are required.

sources.title: Get Validated JSON Results from Models
keyInsights: Bedrock supports native schema-constrained output only for documented APIs and models.
Prompt-only JSON must not be silently treated as native validation.

sources.title: Apply Tags to User Input to Filter Content
keyInsights: Guard only the untrusted portion of mixed trusted and untrusted input.
Static delimiters are injection-prone; request-specific boundaries are safer.

sources.title: Enforce Specific Guardrails in Inference Requests
keyInsights: IAM can deny inference unless a required guardrail and version are present.
Guardrail enforcement belongs at the authorization boundary, not only in prompts.

sources.title: Identity-Based Policy Examples for Amazon Bedrock
keyInsights: Inference access can be limited to exact model or inference-profile resources.
API-only callers do not need console or administrative permissions.

sources.title: LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
keyInsights: Instruction/data separation, least privilege, and output validation must work together.
Prompt text alone is not a sufficient prompt-injection defense.

sources.title: JSON Schema Validation: A Vocabulary for Structural Validation of JSON
keyInsights: Required, enum, uniqueItems, and type constraints have defined validation semantics.
Application invariants such as complete disjoint partitions still require explicit checks.

sources.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
keyInsights: LLM judges exhibit position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases.
Human calibration and order-swapped tests are needed for comparative judgments.

sources.title: Inference Using the OpenAI Responses API
keyInsights: Bedrock Mantle exposes OpenAI-compatible Models and Responses APIs over regional HTTPS endpoints.
Responses storage defaults on, so callers that do not need retrievable state must explicitly send store=false.

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock API Keys
keyInsights: Production use should prefer short-term credentials or the AWS credential chain.
Bearer-token values must not appear in arguments, logs, analytics, or webview state.

sources.title: Data Retention for Amazon Bedrock
keyInsights: Account or project data_retention_mode controls durable request and response handling.
store=false does not independently guarantee zero retention; guaranteed ZDR requires effective mode none.

sources.title: Monitor Model Invocation Using CloudWatch Logs and Amazon S3
keyInsights: Bedrock runtime invocation logging can copy complete prompts and responses when enabled.
The documented invocation-logging feature does not currently capture Responses calls on the bedrock-mantle endpoint.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Sol Model Card
keyInsights: GPT-5.6 Sol is Responses-only on Bedrock Mantle and uses the special /openai/v1 path.
The exact model ID openai.gpt-5.6-sol is available in us-east-1 and us-east-2.

sources.title: API Compatibility by Models
keyInsights: GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna support the Responses API but not Invoke, Converse, or Chat Completions.
API compatibility must be checked per model rather than inferred from provider family.

sources.title: Create a Model Response
keyInsights: The Responses request supports separate instructions and input fields, text.format JSON schema, reasoning effort, output limits, and store=false.
The response status and output_text content must be checked before accepting structured data.

sources.title: reqwest 0.12.28
keyInsights: The async Rust client supports explicit total timeouts, bearer authentication, JSON bodies, redirect policies, and proxy disabling.
Disabling redirects and proxies narrows where a bearer credential can be sent.

sources.title: Calling Rust from the Frontend
keyInsights: Tauri commands expose narrowly typed Rust operations to the frontend.
Result errors reject the frontend promise without exposing a generic process API.

sources.title: Tauri Shell Plugin
keyInsights: Shell execution is dangerous and must be explicitly and narrowly scoped.
A dedicated backend command is safer than exposing arbitrary shell arguments to the webview.

gaps: No human-labeled Trace ML learner-response corpus
No repeated-run or subgroup audit for the selected Bedrock model
The live AWS account mode is provider_data_share rather than guaranteed zero retention
